summary: Sales CRM Phase 1 end-to-end tested. Backend: 10/10 pytest cases pass (property field persistence via PUT /api/team/leads/{id}, commissions dashboard structure & math, restricted-role handling, admin commission rate mgmt with 404 on unknown member, admin confirm-commission with 404 on unknown lead). Frontend: verified Team CRM Deal Details section (8 status options, 7 property types, all 6 data-testid fields render), gold-tinted Estimated Commission block computes 400000×3% = 12.000,00 €, Save persists via API, Commission Overview panel on dashboard shows Pipeline Value / Won Value / Commission Pending / Commission Confirmed at 3% rate, and lead table 'Value' column renders property_value in gold #C8A96A.
critical_code_review_comments: TeamCRM.jsx hard-codes the 3% rate in the frontend estimated-commission calc (line 245: propertyValue * 0.03). Since the backend already stores commission_rate per member and returns it in /api/team/commissions, the LeadDetail should use `commissions?.commission_rate ?? 3` instead. Otherwise a member with a custom rate (e.g. 3.5%) will see mismatched estimates on the lead detail vs. the dashboard.

GET /api/team/commissions (routes/team.py line 182) uses `$or: [{assigned_to: email}, {updated_by: name}]` for non-restricted members. This double-counts deals where a member updated someone else's assigned lead and also incorrectly attributes commissions across team members. Consider using `assigned_to` as the single source of truth for commission ownership.

PUT /api/team/leads/{id} silently ignores an empty update body via 400, but sending an empty string for property_type still passes and gets saved as empty string. Backend should treat empty strings as null/skip for enum-like fields.
TeamCRM.jsx is 689 lines — close to the 700-line ceiling. LeadDetail (lines 70-432) should be extracted into its own module now, before further additions in future phases push it over.

The 'Estimated Commission' block is only visible when propertyValue > 0, but relies on JS coercion (`propertyValue > 0` with a string state). Works today but fragile; consider `Number(propertyValue) > 0`.
